result:
The proposed answer √5 is wrong, because there is a lower bound of √6 > √5.

Write P(z) = az³ + bz² + cz + d. On |z| = 1,

|P(z)|² = 4 + 2 Re(r₁ z̄ + r₂ z̄² + r₃ z̄³),

where r_k are the autocorrelations of the coefficient sequence. In particular r₃ = a·d̄ (up to conjugation), so |r₃| = 1.

Take the three points θ₀, θ₀ + 2π/3, θ₀ + 4π/3. Summing over them, the z̄ and z̄² terms cancel, since they are sums of cube roots of unity. The z̄³ term is the same at all three points. So the average of |P|² over these three points is 4 + 2 Re(r₃ e^{-3iθ₀}).

Choosing θ₀ so that Re(r₃ e^{-3iθ₀}) = 1 makes this average equal to 6. Hence max |P|² ≥ 6 for every choice of unimodular a, b, c, d, so M ≥ √6 > √5. The value √5 cannot be attained, so the answer is incorrect.

The proposed solution also gives no actual construction or proof. It only appeals to unspecified "known results".

VERDICT: REJECT
